title: Cure Allowance by Debt Type of the Placed Account — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
For Hardship and Protective Holds, the days allowed to cure on a cure notice carry a cure debt allowance that depends on the debt type of the placed account the hold request is for, as classified in that account's Placed Consumer Accounts record. Medical and installment creditors supply the itemised statements and payoff letters a completed package often needs. The allowance is added once to the days allowed to cure.

## Client-type schedule

| Debt type of the placed account | Cure debt allowance |
|---|---|
| Medical | 5 calendar days (medical cure days) |
| Auto deficiency | 2 calendar days (installment cure days) |
| Retail installment | 2 calendar days (installment cure days) |
| Private student loan | 2 calendar days (installment cure days) |
| Bank card | None |
| Utility | None |
| Telecom | None |

## Notes

- The debt type is that of the placed account the request is for; the consumer's other accounts do not enter.
- Three debt types share the installment figure of 2 days: auto deficiency, retail installment and private student loan.

**Example (hypothetical).** A cure notice on a request for a hold on a hospital bill placed as a medical debt adds 5 calendar days; the same notice on a utility final bill adds nothing.
